correctness.rationale: P^t=r^t I+(1-r^t)1 pi^T since E^2=E. The stationary joint law Q_v=pi⊗pi+v Delta has Rényi power-sum derivative alpha sum Delta Q^{alpha-1} and second derivative alpha(alpha-1)sum Delta^2 Q^{alpha-2}, strict sign. Cauchy-Schwarz gives B_alpha=sum pi^{2alpha-1}-(sum pi^alpha)^2>=0, equality for non-Shannon alpha only under uniform pi. Curvature and endpoint derivative -infinity for alpha<1 nonuniform guarantee exactly one interior maximum. Shannon relative-entropy curvature and sum Delta^2/(pi_i pi_j)=n-1 establish quadratic deficit; Taylor/implicit function establish near-alpha=1 peak location and height. All strict integer-lag and eventual-overshoot conclusions follow via v=r^t.
residual_risks: All pi_i strictly positive finite n>=2, r in (0,1), stationarity. Interpolation v in [0,1]; a continuous peak need not coincide with integer sampling. No theorem for arbitrary reversible kernels, negative eigenvalues, general divergence monotonicity.
